exposure: group B beta-hemolytic Streptococcus screening during pregnancy
absence of group B beta-hemolytic Streptococcus screening during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 968 pregnant women whose electronic medical records from 2018 to 2022 were searched to evaluate group B beta-hemolytic Streptococcus screening status and perinatal outcomes.
finding: Screening for group B beta-hemolytic Streptococcus was not significantly associated with early-onset neonatal sepsis, but it was an independent predictor of lower prevalence of preterm birth, NICU admission, and neonatal death within 48 hours.
followup_time: 48 hours after birth for neonatal death; other neonatal outcomes were also assessed.
